mensIntro: Men in trades and construction have some of the highest rates of mental health struggles and suicide in Australia — yet they're least likely to seek help. Hazy and Plummo reckon that has to change. These are the organisations making a difference.

mensOrgs.name: Beyond Blue
mensOrgs.desc: Mental health support, resources and a 24/7 helpline for Australians dealing with anxiety and depression.

mensOrgs.name: Black Dog Institute
mensOrgs.desc: Research-led mental health organisation focused on preventing and treating depression, anxiety, PTSD and bipolar disorder.

mensOrgs.name: Heart of the Nation
mensOrgs.desc: The Heart Foundation's initiative supporting the cardiovascular health of Australians — particularly working-age men.

mensOrgs.name: MATES in Construction
mensOrgs.desc: Suicide prevention program specifically developed for the Australian construction and building industry. Built by tradies, for tradies.

mensOrgs.name: MensLine Australia
mensOrgs.desc: Telephone and online support, information and referral service for men with emotional health or relationship concerns.

mensOrgs.name: Lifeline Australia
mensOrgs.desc: 24/7 crisis support and suicide prevention services for all Australians. If you're in crisis, call now.

mensTips.title: 🫁 Dust & Respiratory Health
mensTips.text: Prolonged exposure to fine wood dust — especially from hardwoods — carries serious risks including asthma, sinusitis, and nasal cancers. Always wear a properly rated respirator (P2 or better) when sanding, routing, or machining. Get respiratory checks annually if you're in the trade.

mensTips.title: 👂 Hearing Protection
mensTips.text: Power tools, routers, and planers can exceed 95dB — levels that cause permanent hearing loss within minutes of unprotected exposure. Use rated hearing protection every single time. Once it's gone, it's gone.

mensTips.title: 🦴 Musculoskeletal Health
mensTips.text: Back injuries, shoulder strain, and repetitive stress injuries are endemic in woodworking. Invest in good workshop ergonomics — bench height, anti-fatigue matting, and taking proper breaks. See a physio early; don't push through pain.

mensTips.title: 🧴 Skin & Chemical Exposure
mensTips.text: Finishes, resins, solvents, and timber extractives can cause skin sensitisation and chemical burns. Gloves, long sleeves, and proper ventilation aren't optional — they're standard practice.

womensIntro: Women are a growing and vital part of the Australian woodworking and timber industry. The Timber Bros are committed to highlighting and supporting women's health, wellbeing, and their place in the craft.

womensOrgs.name: Jean Hailes for Women's Health
womensOrgs.desc: Australia's leading women's health organisation — covering everything from hormonal health to mental wellbeing and workplace issues.

womensOrgs.name: 1800RESPECT
womensOrgs.desc: National sexual assault, domestic and family violence counselling service. Available 24/7 — confidential and free.

womensOrgs.name: Beyond Blue — Women
womensOrgs.desc: Mental health support tailored to women's experiences — including postnatal depression, anxiety in the workplace, and more.

womensOrgs.name: Cancer Australia
womensOrgs.desc: Information, support and resources for women facing cancer — particularly breast cancer awareness and screening.

womensOrgs.name: PANDA
womensOrgs.desc: Perinatal Anxiety and Depression Australia — supporting women, men and families affected by perinatal mental health conditions.

womensOrgs.name: Breast Cancer Network Australia
womensOrgs.desc: Industry network supporting women impacted by Breast Cancer — services, support and community.

womensTips.title: 💜 Women's Occupational Health in the Workshop
womensTips.text: Respiratory protection, ergonomic tool sizing, and chemical exposure risks are often calibrated for male bodies. Women should be especially mindful to verify PPE sizing fits correctly, and to seek out research and advice specific to female physiology in trade environments.

womensTips.title: 🌸 Mental Health & Industry Isolation
womensTips.text: Being a woman in a male-dominated industry carries unique pressures. If you're feeling isolated, the Women in Timber network and Beyond Blue both offer community and professional support to help navigate the craft and the workplace.
